result.note: Deal not yet signed, so I tested only the announced headline terms (tariff cut, purchase commitment, duty elimination), anchored to February 2026 and attributed to the announcement.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the India–US trade deal terms announced in February 2026:
items: The US will cut tariffs on Indian goods from 50% to 18%.
India will cut tariffs on US industrial goods from roughly 13.5% to 5%.
India committed to buying USD 500 billion in American goods over five years.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because India will drop tariffs on US industrial goods from roughly 13.5% to zero, not 5%. India plans to meet the USD 500 billion commitment by gradually ramping up purchases of petroleum, aircraft, defence, telecom and pharmaceutical goods.
questions.source: India will drop tariffs on US industrial goods from roughly 13.5% to zero.

questions.prompt: In February 2026, the US Trade Representative described the India–US trade deal terms. Which of the following was among the US products on which India will eliminate duties?
questions.explain: India will eliminate duties on US tree nuts, fruits, vegetables, wine and spirits. The USTR said nothing about rice, beef, soybeans, sugar and dairy, which were also excluded from India's deal with the EU.
questions.source: India will eliminate duties on US tree nuts, fruits, vegetables, wine, and spirits.
